name: BJ the Chicago Kid
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 trap-soul — BJ the Chicago Kid
notes: "Church harmony" is the entry's own heading for the keys line, and it names the cycles: "`i–iv–VII–III` and `IMaj7–vi7–ii7–V7` cycles with gospel passing chords, secondary dominants and a modulating final chorus, played on piano/organ. Real cadences throughout." Both are authored with the sevenths moved into `extensions`, since a numeral here names a degree. ⛔ **`bass808` is null**: "played electric bass with gospel-thumb walking motion on the band material; a long-decay 808 with slides on the rap-facing cuts. Both variants required" — the band variant is the default and is the one that gives him a bass part at all. The kit's stated fingerprint is a timing one: "a live-feel kit with **the snare slightly behind 2&4**, ghost 16ths, tambourine doubling the backbeat, and organ-led stop-time breaks", so `offGridMs` is positive and large, the ghosts are dense and the tambourine mirrors the clap; the stop-time break is the arrangement's high `dropOutBeats`. The vocal is "a warm, gritty mid-tenor with high note-density, long gospel melismatic runs, growl ornament, and choir-wide self-harmonised stacks (his signature is a genuine four-part choir voicing rather than doubled thirds)", which is a high counter ratio weighted onto `sustain_pad` rather than `octave_echo`. ⚠ `confidence` is **low**, mirroring medium-low: "the gospel lineage and collaborations are sourced; parametric detail is inference". ⚠ All drum, swing and bassline numbers are **INFERRED**. ⚠ `session.bpm.mode` is **INFERRED**: the number is not stated in the entry, and it is an authored centre of gravity inside the band the entry does state. ⚠ **`session.keys` is INFERRED.** The entry's Keys line describes the harmonic grammar but names no key centre, so these values and their weights are an authored choice — no key in this set is stated in the research. ⚠ **`drums.kick.lockTo808` removed (2026-08-17, 808 gate).** This kit has no 808 — `bass808` is `null` here or in the parent it inherits — and `lockTo808` is the one parameter that says *how much of the kick the 808 follows*, so in this file it described a pairing that does not exist: `generators::drums::bass808` returns on `block.is_none()` before the value is ever read, which makes it provably dead here. Where it was NOT dead was in the artists and producers who extend this kit and author an 808 of their own: they inherited the zero, `kicks.iter().filter(|_| rng.random_bool(0.0))` kept nothing, and their sub lane was silent at every seed — `bass808::every_shipped_model_with_an_808_produces_a_playable_line` reported "no 808 at all" for 35 of them. Removing it restores the engine's documented default of 1.0 for exactly those children and changes nothing here. ⚠ No researched claim moved: this kit's own statement about the 808 is the `bass808: null` beside it, and that is untouched.
